text:
lisa_support: FYI customers reporting 502/504 + p95 timeouts on hosted inference since ~03:15 UTC. Error spike looks correlated with request queue depth surge.

devon_oncall: Which tenants? any recent deploys? :eyes:

lisa_support: A few high-throughput tenants (acme-inc, foodly, quickserve). No platform deploys between 02:30-03:00 aside from a small infra patch at 01:50 (deploy-bot noted).

mike_runtime: Logs show repeated 'request-queue-timeout' and continuous-batcher backlog growth. sample from gateway: 
```
[E] 03:17:02 gateway: enqueue failed: queue_depth=10240 tenant=acme-inc code=ENQUEUE_LIMIT
[W] 03:17:02 batcher: backlog_size=612 seq_len_avg=128 kv_cache_evictions=178
[E] 03:17:04 router: 504 serve_timeout tenant=acme-inc request_id=rid-7a3
```

anna_sre: Confirming metrics: request_queue_depth p90 -> 11k at 03:16, continuous_batch_backlog p95 -> 580, dequeue rate dropped ~35%.

priya_support: Customers seeing timeouts when they push many short requests in parallel (chatty clients). Repro: small script that fires 200 concurrent short calls gets ~30% 504 within 2m.

devon_oncall: Any KV cache hot-eviction pattern? might be thrashing and slowing batcher.

mike_runtime: KV evictions spike yes, and heavy long-seq jobs are interleaving. Batcher prioritization is falling back to FIFO causing tail buildup. We saw a similar pattern but different root cause last month.

anna_sre: Quick mitigation idea: enable temporary tenant-level ingress rate cap + preferential batching for short seqs. Can we throttle at gateway for acme-inc/foodly?

lisa_support: I can apply a soft throttle per-tenant for the next 15m if you confirm the command.

mike_runtime: Do it. Also flip `batcher.priority_short_requests=true` on the affected pool to prefer short sequences. That should drop backlog.

devon_oncall: Applying throttle now for acme-inc (limit 250 rps burst 500).

ops-bot: Action taken: set_rate_limit tenant=acme-inc rps=250 burst=500 by devon_oncall at 03:28 UTC :white_check_mark:

lisa_support: Noted, customers reporting fewer 504s after throttling, p95 latency improving.

priya_support: Repro attempt post-throttle: same stress script -> 504s down to ~6%. Good improvement.

mike_runtime: We'll still need root cause. Two tracks: 1) tune continuous-batcher prioritization + add short-request fastpath, 2) investigate why dequeue rate fell (worker saturation / kernel sched / network stalls).

anna_sre: I'm collecting traces from 02:45-03:30 and will correlate host CPU + gRPC stall metrics. Uploading perf traces now.

anna_sre: Quick diagnostic result: a small subset of long-sequence inference jobs occupied a disproportionate fraction of GPU queue slots causing batching starvation on others. Also noticed `ephemeral_worker_count` dropped on a few hosts due to kube node oomkill around 02:54.

mike_runtime: OOMs explain worker drop. If workers restart slowly the batcher queues up requests and backlog spikes. Need autoscaling guardrails and faster worker warmup.

devon_oncall: Node oomkill event ID: node-az1-138. kube events show memory pressure from concurrent longseq jobs.

lisa_support: Customer-facing notes: "We throttled traffic and applied mitigations to reduce errors; engineering investigating root cause (node OOMs + batching prioritization)." Can someone draft a short status update?

priya_support: I'll send an interim message to affected tenants with list of mitigations and ETA for next update.

mike_runtime: Action items: (1) implement short-request fastpath in batcher (PR in progress), (2) autoscale worker pool on memory pressure + faster warmup, (3) add tenant-level emergency throttles to playbook, (4) postmortem after stable. Owner: mike_runtime + anna_sre.

devon_oncall: Leaving mitigations in place for 30m and will watch. If p95 > target revert to stricter caps.

lisa_support: Thanks everyone. Marking this thread for postmortem and adding links to traces/metrics: https://grafana.internal/r/abc123 and https://traces.internal/trace/def456

deploy-bot: Note: infra patch at 01:50 was unrelated (config tweak). No rollbacks performed.

anna_sre: Last check at 03:55 UTC: request_queue_depth back below 2k, backlog < 40, p95 within SLA. Closing active escalation; postmortem TBD. :thumbsup:

lisa_support: Closing thread, tracking owners and follow-ups in #postmortems.
